name: St. Helena Plover
rangeDescription: St. helena island (southern atlantic ocean)
description: A long-legged plover with a long black bill, a black eye mask and crown, and a white forehead. Upperparts brownish, and underparts whitish washed with peachy orange.

name: Streak-capped Spinetail
rangeDescription: Santa marta mountains (northeastern colombia)
description: Mostly brown arboreal spinetail with a black-streaked rufous crown and rufous wings and tail. Has a narrow white eyebrow, diffuse pale streaks on face, and slightly downcurved bill.

name: Black-backed Tanager
rangeDescription: Lowlands of southeastern brazil (rio de janeiro to santa catarina)
description: Beautiful multicolored tanager found in coastal forests, forest edges, and gardens where it forages in pairs or small groups. Males are blue-green below with a cinnamon head, black mask, black back, and straw-colored rump, vent, and wing coverts.

name: Arabian Partridge
rangeDescription: Arid regions of southern arabian peninsula to yemen and oman
description: Handsome partridge of southern Arabia. Pale gray overall, with a tan patch on the neck, black-and-white slashes along the sides, and a complicated black-and-white facial pattern.

name: Lewis's Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Oak-pine woodland of western north america; winters to northern mexico
description: A large, social woodpecker with a unique color pattern. Dark glossy-green above with a gray collar, dark red face, and pink wash on the belly.

name: Flores Flowerpecker
rangeDescription: Flores (western lesser sundas)
description: Small and stout forest-dweller that hops and buzzes about in the canopy like a large, active insect. Note male’s iridescent dark blue back, bright red chest, and black line extending down the white belly.

name: Yellow-bellied Dacnis
rangeDescription: Southeastern colombia to southern venezuela, northern bolivia, and western amazonian brazil
description: Small, sharp-billed tanager of tropical lowlands. Males have a black back, bright yellow underparts, and a black mask.

name: Blackish Nightjar
rangeDescription: Eastern colombia to southern venezuela, the guianas, bolivia, and brazil
description: A fairly small, dark nightjar found in the lowlands and foothills of northern South America. Intricately patterned with dark browns and grays; lacks any obvious features like a collar (although it sometimes shows a small white patch on the side of the neck).

name: White-collared Foliage-gleaner
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (minas gerais and espírito santo to eastern santa catarina)
description: Large foliage-gleaner with a wedge-shaped bill. Found in the middle and lower levels of forests with bamboo where it acrobatically hangs upside-down on branches and searches for prey in clusters of dead leaves.

name: Blue-capped Hummingbird
rangeDescription: Southern mexico (sierra de miahuatlán of oaxaca)
description: Endemic and distinctive, medium-sized hummingbird found in the foothills of the Sierra Madre del Sur in Oaxaca. Favors humid evergreen forests and shade-coffee plantations.

name: Acre Antshrike
rangeDescription: Western amazonian brazil in serra do divisor national park
description: Secretive, rare medium-sized antshrike of the dense forests of the Cordillera Divisor of remote western Brazil and eastern Peru. Males are dark gray with a bluish tint to the back and upperparts, while females are bluish-gray above and brownish-orange below.

name: Tiny Sunbird
rangeDescription: Sierra leone to cameroon, gabon, eastern democratic republic of the congo, and western uganda; bioko
description: The smallest member of a group of frustratingly similar double-collared sunbirds that co-occur in African forests. Often encountered near forest edges and in forest clearings, and sometimes even in villages and gardens.

name: Chestnut-backed Owlet
rangeDescription: Forest of wet zone of sri lanka
description: Small owl lacking ear tufts, with chestnut mantle and pale belly with streaked flanks. Crepuscular and diurnal, occurring singly or in pairs in wet rainforest, or neighboring woods.

name: Santa Cruz Ground Dove
rangeDescription: Tinakula and utupua (northern and central temotu, southeastern solomon islands), and vanuatu
description: A rotund, short-legged ground-dwelling dove that usually runs rather than flies when startled. Male has a dark body with an iridescent pinkish-purple shoulder patch, a cream-colored chest, and a gray head.

name: Bamboo Antshrike
rangeDescription: Local from southeastern peru to northwestern bolivia and southwestern amazonian brazil
description: Small antshrike of bamboo thickets in lowland rainforest. Found primarily in bamboo forests, but occasionally also in other densely vegetated thickets such as vine tangles and cane stands.

name: Española Ground-Finch
rangeDescription: Española (galapagos)
description: A large and stout-billed Galápagos finch confined to the island of Española. Identification is straightforward, since the only other finches living on Española (Small Ground-Finch and Gray Warbler-Finch) have relatively tiny bills.

name: Yellow-footed Honeyguide
rangeDescription: Sierra leone to liberia, southwestern ghana, and southwestern cameroon
description: Medium-sized honeyguide with a plain face, a slim pale bill, yellow legs, and large white patches in the outer tail. Found in the middle levels and canopy of humid forest at low and middle elevations.

name: Parodi's Hemispingus
rangeDescription: Andes of southeastern peru (cusco)
description: Small olive-yellow tanager with a dingy brown face and crown and a yellow eyebrow. Found in humid elfin forest in the southern Peruvian Andes, where it forages singly or in pairs, often joining mixed-species flocks with other tanagers, flowerpiercers, and hemispinguses.

name: Speckled Rail
rangeDescription: Locally in lowlands of south america east of the andes
description: Very rare and poorly known, but likely widely overlooked, small rail of the southern cone from SE Brazil to central Argentina. Its secretive nature makes it difficult to understand its habitat and habits, but timing of records, combined with records from the middle of downtown Buenos Aires and São Paolo, suggest it is at least somewhat migratory.

name: Yellow-rumped Serin
rangeDescription: Savanna of eritrea and northern ethiopia
description: A very plain gray-brown seedeater with a white throat and a yellow rump that is conspicuous in flight. Found locally in savanna, woodland, and cultivated areas, usually in small flocks.
